observation.visible_scene: A tranquil, narrow forest river/stream viewed from a fixed position. Lush green deciduous trees line both banks, meeting in the middle distance where the water narrows and shows a small stretch of faster-flowing surface. The calm foreground water mirrors the bright sky and the tree canopy. A single grey rock protrudes from the surface left-of-center, and a fallen log lies along the right bank. Two persistent lens-flare artifacts are visible: a pale green disc in the upper-left and a reddish-orange streak in the lower-left. The framing of all background elements (trees, rock, log, flares) is identical across every frame, indicating no camera translation or zoom.
visible_changes: The water surface undergoes continuous, low-amplitude motion: fine ripples and shimmer appear and shift across the foreground, subtly deforming the reflected sky and tree images (e.g., the central tree reflection breaks up and re-forms slightly between frames).
Small pale floating particles/foam scattered on the left portion of the water drift and redistribute their pattern over time.
The distant flowing section of the stream keeps moving steadily, consistent with an ongoing current rather than a start or stop.
The rock, log, trees, and lens-flare artifacts remain in fixed screen positions, confirming the camera is stationary and these are not moving objects.
outside_clip_unknowns: The physical cause of the surface ripples (wind, current, or a disturbance outside the frame) is not shown.
Whether the tree foliage sways at all is not resolvable; no clear leaf motion is visible.
What precedes or follows this excerpt is unknown; the flow and rippling are already underway at frame 1 and continue at frame 41 with no onset or completion.
uncertain_details: Any camera micro-jitter is indistinguishable from the static framing given the fixed background and flare positions.
The white specks on the water could be foam, pollen, or floating debris; their identity is not confirmable.
Differences between adjacent frames are very subtle, so ripple 'motion' is inferred from cumulative change across the sequence rather than from any single frame pair.
